See our privacy policy . Common garage door questions How much does it cost to fix a garage door in Brisbane? + It depends on the door type and the fault. Minor adjustments and opener fixes often sit in the low hundreds of dollars, while spring, cable or motor replacement costs more. Because labour rates and access at your property affect the figure, the specialist gives you a written, fixed-price quote before any work starts, and the figures on this site are indicative only. Why won't my garage door close properly? + A door that will not close or keeps reversing is usually a safety-sensor problem: the photo-eyes near the bottom of the tracks are misaligned, dirty or obstructed. Worn rollers, a bent track or the opener's force and travel settings can also be the cause. Clearing the sensor path is worth a try, but a persistent fault needs a technician to check the tracks, sensors and opener settings. Is a broken garage door spring safe to use? + No. The spring carries most of the door's weight, so a broken one makes the door heavy, unbalanced and unsafe to operate. Forcing it with the opener can bend tracks, strain the motor or drop the door. Stop using the door and have the spring replaced by a technician, who uses the right tools to unwind and reset the tension safely. Do I need a licensed electrician for a garage door motor? + Any mains-voltage wiring, new power points or hard-wired connections for a powered opener must legally be carried out by a licensed electrician in Queensland under the Electrical Safety Act 2002. Mechanical work on the door, springs and tracks does not need an electrician. The specialists in our Brisbane network coordinate both, so the electrical side is always handled by a licensed electrician.
